title: The palace hotels of the Belle Époque
episode: Nice, France: The Belle Époque - Rick Steves’ Europe Travel Guide - Travel Bite
description: A short piece on Nice’s Belle Époque, when European royalty wintered here and grand hotels rose along the Promenade des Anglais, a seafront path first paid for by English residents in the 1820s. The Negresco opened in 1913.

title: A cathedral built for the Russian court
episode: Nice - the Russian Cathedral is reborn
description: St. Nicholas Cathedral, finished in 1912 for the Russian aristocrats who wintered in Nice, is the largest Russian Orthodox church in Western Europe. This report shows its restoration in the 2010s.

title: The Riviera in the 1920s
description: A minute of travel footage from the 1920s, when Americans and artists made the Riviera a summer destination. The Palais de la Méditerranée, a casino on the Promenade, opened in 1929.

title: The man who broke the bank at Monte Carlo
episode: The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo
description: The story of Charles Wells, a British con man who won a fortune at roulette in Monte Carlo in 1891 and inspired a popular song. Monaco, a tiny independent state, is 20 minutes east of Nice by train.

title: Matisse in his own words, 1941
episode: Chatting with Henri Matisse: The Lost 1941 Interview
description: A program on a long interview Matisse gave in Nice in 1941, recovered and published decades later. He lived and worked in an apartment in the Régina, a hotel built for Queen Victoria’s visits.

title: Matisse’s chapel at Vence
episode: MATISSE'S CHAPELLE DU ROSAIRE DE VENCE, FRANCE
description: A short look inside the Rosary Chapel, which Matisse designed for Dominican nuns in Vence and finished in 1951. Its white tiles and blue, green, and yellow stained glass fill the small room with colored light.

title: Yves Klein, the painter of blue
episode: MAMAC – Yves Klein, the master of blue
description: The city’s film on Yves Klein, born in Nice in 1928, who registered his own shade of ultramarine. He said he signed the sky over Nice as his first artwork. The modern art museum on Place Yves Klein holds many of his works.

title: Socca from the market
episode: Chez Theresa - Socca - Cours Saleya - Nice
description: Socca, a thin pancake of chickpea flour and olive oil, baked in a wood-fired oven and sold in paper. Chez Thérésa has sold it at the Cours Saleya market for decades.

title: The real salade niçoise
episode: The ORIGINS OF NIÇOISE SALAD | Sea, Scandals & Sun
description: A Nice guide on the origins of the salade niçoise, and on the rules locals defend: tomatoes, anchovies or tuna, eggs, olives, and raw vegetables, but no potatoes and no green beans.

title: After the attack of July 14
episode: France: Living with the aftermath of Nice's terror attack
description: A report on Nice after July 14, 2016, when a man drove a truck into the crowds watching Bastille Day fireworks on the Promenade, killing 86 people.
